note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: ProcessStep (buffered_streaming_detokenizer.cc:105-192 at b7b856a0) still re-decodes on new tokens, trims U+FFFD, and releases the unreleased part of the LCP of previous and current decodes cut back off a multi-byte sequence; but our 53a08cb1 and 9be98b62 (2026-11-13, both in the release Agello ships) add release_first_decode (header 48-54, default false): with it, the first valid decode is released at once up to the LCP of the decode and the decode of the IDs repeated twice, when that prefix ends in an ASCII byte; otherwise the first step waits. DecodeOneStep always constructs the detokenizer with release_first_decode=true (tasks.cc:216-221), so in the decode loop the one-step lag applies only when that check fails.
corrected_text: BufferedStreamingDetokenizer::ProcessStep re-decodes a head's accumulated token IDs on each step that brings new tokens for it (with no new tokens it reuses the previous decode), trims trailing U+FFFD replacement characters, and releases only the not-yet-released part of the longest common prefix of the previous and current decodes, cut back so it never ends inside a valid multi-byte UTF-8 sequence. While the previous decode was empty it releases nothing (one-step lag), unless the detokenizer was built with release_first_decode, as the decode loop's always is in our build and the release Agello ships (ours: 53a08cb1, 9be98b62): then it releases the first decode at once, up to the text that the IDs repeated twice still decode to, if that text ends in an ASCII character.
